source.title: Characterizing Verbatim Short-Term Memory in Neural Language Models
source.authors: Kristijan Armeni; C. Honey; Tal Linzen

page_placements.theme: Verbatim in-context retrieval as short-term or episodic memory (behavioural)

record.tranche_reason: The study measures verbatim retrieval of repeated noun lists, but does not identify or test induction heads, the [A][B] … [A] → [B] mechanism, or in-context learning by token position. It mentions induction heads in its discussion and suggests verbatim memory could support in-context learning.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on repeated-list surprisal and attention-dependent retrieval. These do not establish that induction heads were present or that retrieval was the claimed induction-head behavior. Its discussion of induction heads refers to prior work; cited results are not recorded as findings from this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures how much surprisal drops when a noun list repeats in pretrained or trained LMs. It never identifies attention heads, previous-token composition, training dynamics, or loss by token index. Induction heads appear only in the Discussion, citing Olsson et al. as concurrent work. The attention-shuffle ablation is applied uniformly to all layers, not to specific heads. The authors themselves defer head-level ablations to future work. So the results show a related behavioural construct (verbatim copying) without testing any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that transformers retrieve individual prior tokens and their order. Retrieval improves with corpus size and depth and depends on learned attention. The LSTM keeps an order-insensitive semantic gist that decays quickly. They speculate this memory may underpin in-context learning, citing Olsson et al.'s induction heads as concurrent work.
record.recipe_differences: Measures surprisal on repeated noun lists in trained language models; it does not locate induction heads, test previous-token-head composition, or track training-time transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: Retrieval varies with corpus size, transformer depth, attention disruption, list type, and intervening-text conditions. The reported robustness to vignette phrasing differs between GPT-2 and the Wikitext-103 transformer.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-2 (WebText) shows near-complete verbatim and order-sensitive retrieval of repeated noun lists: 2% repeat surprisal vs 58% permuted and 96% novel. The same architecture trained on Wikitext-103 shows much weaker retrieval (88/92/99%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Order-sensitive in-context copying of repeated sequences in transformer LMs grows strongly with training corpus size.

fits_no_version.finding: 1- and 3-layer Wikitext-103 transformers show modest recall but no order sensitivity (85% for both repeated and permuted lists in the 3-layer model). Order sensitivity emerges at 6 and 12 layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In natural-text-trained transformers on a small corpus, order-sensitive copying requires more depth than the 2-layer minimum reported for induction heads.

fits_no_version.finding: Permuting key/query rows in every GPT-2 attention layer raises repeat surprisal from 3% to 90% and removes order sensitivity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned attention patterns are necessary for verbatim, order-sensitive retrieval in GPT-2.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
record.problems: The study's measure is repeated-list surprisal rather than induction-head activity or token-index in-context learning. It does not test the claimed training-time transition. Some model-depth outcomes are described qualitatively in the text, with exact values available only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Other noun-list conditions, including set sizes, intervening-text lengths and types, and vignette phrasing controls in Figures 2–7, were not itemized because they report related memory-retrieval conditions rather than any of the claim versions. The LSTM results were also outside the transformer-specific claim.

untested.parts: No heads identified; no previous-token-head composition or head-level [A][B]…[A]→[B] test.
No training checkpoints; no phase change or loss bump measured.
No loss-by-token-index ICL measure and no attribution of ICL to heads.
No head-level induction behaviour across models. Behavioural copying is compared across a transformer and an LSTM only.
Corpus size and depth effects are on list retrieval, not on induction-head formation or ICL persistence.

record.verdict_notes: Row states of cannot_determine with versions ['none'] are appropriate. The randomly initialized transformer control in Fig. 8 is not rowed and rows_left_out does not declare it. It bears on no version, so it is not listed as missing. The behavioural measure resembles the induction signature, but without head identification it cannot support or challenge V1–V7.

versions.untested_parts: No induction heads were identified or tested; no composition with a previous-token head or [A][B] … [A] → [B] completion was measured.
No training-time induction-head formation, in-context-learning gain, or associated loss-curve bump was measured.
No token-index in-context-learning measure or test of how much ICL induction heads carry was reported.
The study did not test for induction behaviour across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
The study varied corpus/model settings for noun-list retrieval, not induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
The study did not test mechanisms of few-shot task learning or compare induction heads with other few-shot mechanisms.
No stages or sub-steps of induction-head formation were measured.

relation.reason: The Discussion connects verbatim memory to in-context learning and describes concurrent induction-head research; its own experiments do not test induction heads.

tranche.reason: The study measures noun-list retrieval without identifying induction heads or testing any claim version's mechanism or training dynamics.

source_check.notes: Repeat surprisal averages over non-initial nouns; Figure 3 reports medians with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. The authors explicitly leave depth versus parameter count unresolved.
